sections.h2: What does the Yadkin County Register of Deeds handle?
sections.html:
This office in Yadkinville keeps the county's land records: deeds, deeds of trust, maps and related filings. State law opens those records to public inspection. The staff also copy and certify birth, death and marriage certificates, issue marriage licenses and swear in notaries.

A sale is only fully protected once the deed is on the books. Under G.S. 47-18, an unregistered conveyance loses to lien creditors and later buyers who paid value, and whoever registers first generally ranks first.

The county web page urges electronic recording for every document. Marriage licenses and notary oaths run by appointment through 336-849-7904. Yadkin County voters choose the register of deeds, and that same office takes the deed excise tax at the time of recording.

sections.h2: How does a deed get on record after a Yadkin County sale?
sections.html:
Usually the attorney or title company at the closing table sends it electronically. The register accepts every document type except maps by e-recording. Any firm wanting to submit must go through Simplifile, CSC or ePN and complete a submitter agreement that the provider passes to the county.

The Yadkin County tax office page has a one-line instruction for deed work: consult your attorney, then it links to the Register of Deeds. Sellers in Yadkinville, Jonesville, East Bend or on a rural road in between therefore rarely deal with the recording desk themselves.

  • Ask whether your closing firm already has an e-recording agreement with Yadkin County.
  • Find out who is writing the check for the excise tax, since the statute assigns it to the seller.
  • Keep the recording confirmation as proof of the date and time of registration.
  • Bringing paper instead? Phone the office before you drive, because no walk-in recording hours appear on the county page.

sections.h2: What does recording cost at the Yadkin County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
A single statewide schedule applies here. G.S. 161-10 prints one schedule for the whole state, calls it complete and exclusive, and requires payment up front.

Selected recording fees printed in G.S. 161-10
What is filedCharge
Deed or other general instrument (pages 1 to 15)$26.00
Mortgage or deed of trust (pages 1 to 35)$64.00
Every page past those ranges$4.00
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo fee
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 per added page
Nonstandard document$25.00 extra
Additional instrument within one document$10.00

Count the pages in your deed and exhibits before closing, because the $4.00 charge starts on the sixteenth page of a general instrument.

sections.h2: Who owes the excise stamp on a Yadkin County deed?
sections.html:
The person transferring the house. G.S. 105-228.30 sets a levy of $1.00 for each $500.00, with any leftover fraction counted as another $500.00, applied to the price or value of the interest conveyed. Payment is due at the register's counter ahead of the filing.

Collections are divided evenly. Yadkin County keeps its half, and the other half moves to the Department of Revenue every month after refunds and an allowance, with the county entitled to hold back 2 percent of the state share. The closing statement lists the dollar figure that applies to your price.

If a house passes as a gift or between relatives, ask the office how a stated value is treated before anyone signs.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Yadkin County tax bills and the 2027 revaluation?
sections.html:
The Yadkin County Tax Department lists, appraises and bills real and personal property, handles exemption applications and maintains ownership records and parcel maps. Its web page announces that a 2027 revaluation is underway.

  • Pay online, by phone at 866-249-4184 with the year and bill number, by mail to P.O. Box 1217, Yadkinville, or at the tax office in the Magnolia building across from the courthouse at 101 South State Street.
  • Questions go to 110 E Elm or 336-849-7903, Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
  • Taxes paid in August earn a 2 percent discount.
  • The rate list also shows a solid waste fee of $76.00 per household, or $38.00 with the elderly exemption.

State law sets September 1 as the due date and begins interest on January 6, at 2 percent through February 1 and three-fourths of 1 percent per month afterward (G.S. 105-360).

sections.h2: Which tax relief programs can follow a Yadkin County homeowner into a sale?
sections.html:
The deferral under the circuit breaker is the program that can surprise a seller. It limits tax to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent when income exceeds the limit but stays under 150 percent of it, and it parks the difference as a lien. A transfer triggers payment of the deferred amounts for the three prior years.

The elderly or disabled exclusion and the disabled veteran exclusion work by lowering the assessed value instead. The first takes off $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value, whichever is greater, for owners under the $38,800 income cap that applies to 2026. The second removes $45,000 and has no age or income test. A household takes only one of the three, applies to the county tax office, and may file up to June 1 before the tax year.

Statutes: 105-277.1B, 105-277.1 and 105-277.1C.

sections.h2: What does the Yadkin County housing picture look like?
sections.html:
Yadkin County counted 38,325 people in mid-2025, up 3.0 percent from the 2020 estimates base and still a little under its 2010 census figure of 38,406. About 111 people live on each of its 334.94 land square miles, and there are 17,697 housing units.

Owners live in 76.9 percent of Yadkin County homes. The five-year survey for 2020 to 2024 gives $181,200 as the middle home value, $1,177 a month in costs for owners with a mortgage and $766 in rent. Households earn a median $62,932, and 14.5 percent of people fall below the poverty line. Adults 65 and over are 22.4 percent of residents and 1,966 are veterans, so the age-based and veteran programs reach many owners.

The county had 650 employer establishments and 8,235 jobs in 2023, and workers travel 29.6 minutes on average to reach work. New construction is slow, with 116 building permits in 2025. Resales of inherited and older houses make up much of the activity, and for an estate sale the clerk of superior court can tell you who has authority to sign.

sections.h2: What happens when Yadkin County forecloses for unpaid taxes?
sections.html:
The county sues on the tax lien, serves the record owner, the spouse and other lienholders, then auctions the parcel at the courthouse door. The winning bidder gets fee simple title free of most liens and pays recording fees and stamps when the deed is registered.

After a sale, a commissioner reports within three days, and an increased bid or exceptions can be filed within 10 days of that report. Redemption stays open until confirmation, on payment of the tax, penalties, interest and costs (G.S. 105-374). Sales are posted on the county's Tax Foreclosure Sales page.

faqs.q: Will a Yadkin County sale trigger a transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes, North Carolina's deed excise tax, which the seller pays at the register of deeds before the deed is filed. The statute charges $1.00 per $500.00 of value, counting a leftover fraction as a full unit.

faqs.q: Can my Yadkin County deed be recorded electronically?
faqs.a: Yes, unless the document is a map. Your attorney or title company needs a submitter agreement through Simplifile, CSC or ePN first. For a paper filing, call 336-849-7904 to ask how the office wants it submitted.

faqs.q: How do I pay a Yadkin County property tax bill?
faqs.a: You can pay online, by telephone at 866-249-4184, by mail to P.O. Box 1217 in Yadkinville, or in person at the tax office in the Magnolia building on South State Street. August payments receive a 2 percent discount.

faqs.q: What does a deed of trust cost to record in Yadkin County?
faqs.a: A mortgage filing runs $64.00 through page 35, then $4.00 per page beyond that. The schedule is statewide under G.S. 161-10, and satisfactions of a deed of trust carry no fee.

faqs.q: Is a Yadkin County revaluation coming?
faqs.a: Yes, the county tax page says a 2027 revaluation is underway. Counties must reappraise all real estate on an eight-year cycle at the longest.
